observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a clear, rectangular (emerald-cut) faceted diamond standing upright on a glossy black reflective surface against a near-black background dotted with blurred blue light spots; a mirror image of the stone is visible directly below it.
visible_changes: At the very start a faint thin vertical light streak hangs above the stone and is gone by t=0.08s.
A bright white flare with rainbow chromatic rays first blooms on the upper-right edge of the diamond (t=0.04-0.08s).

The dominant light then moves to the left edge, producing long red/orange/yellow/green/blue beams that streak across the stone, intensifying through t=0.20-0.48s (peak around t=0.44-0.48s) and fading by t=0.68s.

The diamond's apparent orientation rotates slowly and continuously: the tilt of its table and internal facet lines shifts gradually from frame 1 to frame 41, with the reflection below rotating in sync.
The blurred blue bokeh in the background drifts from the right side toward the upper-left over the clip.
In the latter half (t=1.36-1.56s) small star-like sparkle points appear along the diamond's upper edges while the broad beams have faded.
outside_clip_unknowns: The source or mechanism of the moving colored light beam.
Whether the diamond is on a turntable or the viewpoint is orbiting.
What occurs before t=0 and after t=1.6s.
uncertain_details: Whether the changing facet tilt is physical rotation of the stone or a camera/viewpoint change.
The exact nature of the initial thin vertical streak (light ray vs. object).
Whether background bokeh drift reflects camera motion or light-source motion.
